The Passing Away of Ramanand Swami

On 17 December 1801, while meditating, Ramanand Swami passed away and went to Akshardham. Divine light emanated all around.

As news spread of Ramanand Swami’s demise, thousands of devotees became overwhelmed with grief. 

Although in mourning, Sahajanand Swami consoled everyone, “Great souls never leave this world. By obeying Swami’s commands, one will not feel that he has departed, and one will come to realise the manifest form of God.” 

Exactly 31 days had elapsed since Ramanand Swami had passed on the reins to Sahajanand Swami in Jetpur.

After six years of unflinching dedication and thousands of hours of volunteer work, Sadguru Pujya Kothari Swami (Pujya Bhaktipriya Swami) performed the consecration ceremony at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, in Chino Hills, California.

Constructed from 35,000 pieces of meticulously hand carved Italian Carrara Marble and Indian Pink Sandstone, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Chino Hills, houses five pinnacles, two large domes, four balconies, 122 pillars and 129 archways. From the external walls and domes to the internal pillars and ceilings, the Mandir is completely etched with intricate carvings in marble and sandstone. 

The 6,600 hand-carved motifs depict a mosaic of tales of inspiration, devotion and dedication, along with historical figures from Hindu Dharma. Artisans created the carvings in India with great love, skill and patience before the pieces were shipped to Chino Hills. 

The Mandir is situated on a 20-acre site, complete with a 91-foot lotus-shaped reflection pond, a Cultural Centre, gymnasium and classrooms.

As the first earthquake-proof mandir in the world, the upper structure of the complex is protected from earthquake damage by separating it from the base with a series of 40 base-isolator units. 

The Mandir also uses a solar power system to generate electricity and reduce adverse effects on the environment. The Mandir combines the best of traditional stone art and architecture and the best of modern technology.

Swaminarayan Mahamantra

An aspirant named Shitaldas arrived in the village of Faneni hoping to have darshan of Ramanand Swami. On arrival, he was saddened to learn that Ramanand Swami had passed away a few days earlier on 17 December. 

He soon met Sahajanand Swami, who told him to chant a mantra. It was a new mantra he had just introduced to all in the assembly while explaining the dharma to be observed by the followers of the Sampradaya.

On chanting the 'Swaminarayan' mahamantra, Shitaldas attained samadhi in which he entered Akshardham, where he saw Sahajanand Swami himself as Paramatma, the supreme avatari of all avatars.

Awakening from samadhi, Shitaldas narrated his experience to everyone. 

Revealing the glory of the mantra, Bhagwan Swaminarayan said, "This is the supreme mantra, and it represents our upasana. Whoever recites it will be freed of all miseries and will attain Akshardham."

Gradually, the glory of this mantra spread everywhere and soon, Sahajanand Swami became popularly known as Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

Today, that mantra is chanted daily by countless the world over.

The turn of the millennium.

Devotees in London gathered on 31 December 1999 at the mandir in London for a special devotional programme to usher in a new year and the new millennium.

After a fun-filled programme, the sabha was connected by phone live in the early hours of the morning to Chennai, where Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj was engaged in his morning walk.

2 January 1940
Sarangpur, India

On this day, Shanti Bhagat (later known as Pramukh Swami Maharaj) stepped foot on the sanctified soil of Sarangpur for the first time ever.

After studying for a month in Bhadran, the student sadhus were called to Ahmedabad to attend the parayan organised during the month of Magshar in December 1939 CE. Following the parayan, Shastriji Maharaj asked Shanti Bhagat: "Have you had darshan of Sarangpur Mandir?"
Hearing Shanti Bhagat's reply of "no," Shastriji Maharaj said, "I want to arrange for you to have darshan of Sarangpur. Come with me."

When Shanti Bhagat asked Shastriji Maharaj if he should inform Hariswarupdas, Shastriji Maharaj replied, "What's the need in asking him? You come." However, thinking it would be better to ask since he was staying with Hariswarupdas, Shanti Bhagat approached him and informed him of his plans. Hariswarupdas became angry and threatened, "If you go, I will not let you come back to Bhadran. You are not to go." Shanti Bhagat, shocked by this response, approached Shastriji Maharaj for a solution. Shastriji Maharaj spoke to Hariswarupdas, saying, "This bhagat is still new and wants to visit Sarangpur, so let him go." Thus, Shastriji Maharaj personally took Shanti Bhagat to Sarangpur.

On Tuesday 2 January 1940, Shanti Bhagat arrived in Sarangpur for the first time. The blessed land was delighted to welcome the one who was to later make this his eternal home.

Shanti Bhagat was overjoyed to see the beautiful, sky-touching mandir of Sarangpur. Seeing this masterpiece created by Shastriji Maharaj, he realised his glory even further. Shastriji Maharaj explained to Shanti Bhagat the greatness of this place and the murtis in the mandir.

Ever since that day, Sarangpur held a special place in the mind of Shanti Bhagat. Such was the good fortune of Sarangpur!

A few days later, Shastriji Maharaj took Shanti Bhagat to Gondal, where the young parshads was overjoyed to have darshan of Akshar Mandir for the first time.

It was at the sacred Akshar Deri there that he would be given bhagvati diksha by Shastriji Maharaj on the morning of 10 January 1940.

18 January 1932
Gondal, India

Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj consecrated the first two Akshar-Purushottam mandirs in Bochasan (1907) and Sarangpur (1916).

At the holy Akshar Deri in Gondal, senior sadgurus from Junagadh toyed with the idea of building a small mandir over the Akshar Deri.

In the summer of 1931, Gunatitanand Swami gave darshan to some devotees to develop the site in Gondal.

Devotees loyal to Naranji Maharaj of Zadeshwar acquired land from the Maharaja of Gondal under stringent conditions. 

They then turned to Shastriji Maharaj to fulfil those conditions and handed over the land.

Knowing it to be the wish of Maharaj and Swami, Shastriji Maharaj assured them the conditions would be fulfilled, namely the mandir be completed within three years using stone procured locally with a spend of ten lakh rupees as well as keeping the Akshar Deri intact.

Shastriji Maharaj, Nirgundas Swami and Yogiji Maharaj inspired hundreds of devotees to attend the historic groundbreaking ceremony.

20 January 1810 CE 
Posh sud Punam, VS 1866
Dabhan, India

Bhagwan Swaminarayan held a grand yagna in Dabhan in January 1810. On the concluding day of the yagna, he ordained 25-year-old Mulji Sharma of Bhadra into the sadhu-fold.

Amidst Vedic mantras and boundless joy, Bhagwan Swaminarayan named Mulji 'Gunatitanand Swami', revealing: "He is the manifest form of Akshardham, my abode. I am extremely delighted to ordain him. In the future, his name ‘Gunatitanand’ will become universally known.”

Bhagwan Swaminarayan's words have come true today. 

Today, the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam - Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami along with Bhagwan Swaminarayan - have been consecrated in the central shrines of hundreds of mandirs around the world.

Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami was the first spiritual successor of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the personified form of his divine abode, Akshardham.

Vedic Shastras, including the Bhagavad Gita, Brahma Sutras and the Upanishads, explain the infinite glory of Aksharbrahma. 

While on this earth, Gunatitanand Swami selflessly served Bhagwan Swaminarayan and explained Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s greatness to thousands of devotees. 

Similarly, Bhagwan Swaminarayan revealed Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami’s glory on many occasions.

Authored by Adi Acharya Shri Raghuvirji Maharaj of Vadtal and composed by Achintyanand Brahmachari, the Harililakalpataru shastra extols the supreme glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan as Parabrahma Purushottam Narayan and Gunatitanand Swami as Aksharbrahma.

The below verse from the Harililakalpataru describes one such occasion, on this historic day in Dabhan, when Bhagwan Swaminarayan revealed Gunatitanand Swami's spiritual greatness: 

Mulji-sharmane dīkshām dadānasya prajāyate I
Bhuyān-metra samānando yato Dhāmāksharam cha me II

‘I am extremely happy to initiate Mulji Sharma. He is my divine abode, Akshardham.’ 
Harililakalpataru 7.17.49

Bhagwan Swaminarayan also prophesied on that day that this new initiate would become famed throughout the world by the name of ‘Gunatitanand’.

Gunatitānanda-rupam vishva-khyātam bhavishyati II
Harililakalpataru 7.17.54

Pramukh Swami Maharaj departed with nine sadhus amid a joyous farewell for his first Satsang tour abroad after becoming guru in 1971. The plane took off from Mumbai at 10.15am and landed in Nairobi at 1.22pm. As the passengers disembarked, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the sadhus were ordered to stay aboard. Then, at 4.15pm, without any reason, they were instructed to fly back to Mumbai. Everyone in the group was saddened by the unexpected order to return. 

When Pujya Kothari Swami gave his diary to Swamishri during their flight back to Mumbai, he wrote, "The wish of Maharaj [Bhagwan Swaminarayan] and Bapa [Yogiji Maharaj] prevails. So, one should remain happy. Accept the ways they desire for you. Do not be pained or become miserable. Become aksharrup and offer devotion to God, then one will not be miserable."

At 2.45am Swamishri arrived in Mumbai. After reaching the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Dadar, he offered prostrations to the small murti of Thakorji, Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. Swamishri asked for his forgiveness in not being able to offer him food (thal) during their return journey to Mumbai. Swamishri had a fresh meal prepared at night and offered it to Thakorji while singing thal.

The following morning, Swamishri discoursed in a buoyantly jovial manner, inspiring laughter and joy in all the sadhus and devotees, thus making all forget the misery of having to return.

Beginnings of Akshar Deri in Gondal

Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami passed away to Akshardham in Gondal on 11 October 1867.

Following the agnisanskar rites on the banks of the River Gondali, his sacred ashes (asthi) were collected in a copper urn. Work soon started to construct a chhatri at the sacred site. This chhatri was completed in two months and was inaugurated on the auspicious day of Vasant Panchmi.

Known as the 'Akshar Deri', this chhatri marked the samadhi sthan of Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami.

The holy charanarvind of Bhagwan Swaminarayan were consecrated at this site followed by the pictorial murtis of Akshar-Purushottam. This shrine soon became a place of pilgrimage, fulfilling the wishes of countless devotees.

In 1934, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj opened 'Akshar Mandir' built over the sacred Akshar Deri. This has now become a popular place of pilgrimage, frequented by devotees all over the world.

5 February 1983
Sundalpura, India

It was past six in the morning in the village of Sundalpura near Anand. Pramukh Swami Maharaj had a jam-packed programme ahead. Whilst bathing, he made no mention of the tightness in his chest, nor gave any physical clue. 

While attending to his morning routine, Swamishri was overcome with pain and started to sweat profusely. The sadhus rushed to him. He was suffering a heart attack at the age of 62. With no medical facilities available in the village, plans were soon made to transfer Swamishri to Dr. B.R. Patel's hospital in Vadodara, almost 50km away.

While Swamishri was being rushed to Vadodara in a high speed convoy of cars, his car suddenly screeched to a halt at a crossroad. Fearing the worst, everyone ran to Swamishri’s car. Swamishri appeared calm yet concerned. He called for Acharya Swami and told him, “Tomorrow, we were scheduled to attend the Shikshapatri parayan at Dahyabhai Gajjar’s place in Anand. Please go there and ensure that everything is taken care of. And explain why I won’t be able to come...”

It is common medical knowledge that the first few hours after a heart attack are probably one of the most critical periods that any patient can ever face. 

Senior swamis, Mahant Swami and Dr Swami, both cancelled their vicharan, and also rushed to Vadodara to ensure that Swamishri received appropriate treatment. 

When Mahant Swami first saw Swamishri, he was hooked up to life support systems. In this state, Swamishri beckoned an attendant near and whispered, "Make sure you prepare mag for Mahant Swami."

19 March 1821 
Fagan Vad 1
Panchala, India

In 1821, Bhagwan Swaminarayan was in the village of Panchala, Gujarat, to celebrate the Holi festival. 

He gave all the sadhus a small piece of sandalwood each. The following morning, Bhagwan Swaminarayan did not see a tilak on any foreheads. After further inquiry, he found that the sadhus had consumed the sandalwood, thinking it to be prasad. He distributed another piece and instructed them to perform a tilak.

The next day, he saw that the sadhus had applied tilaks of different shapes and sizes.

Bhagwan Swaminarayan then requested Gunatitanand Swami to come forward. With his own hands, Bhagwan Swaminarayan applied a sandalwood tilak and a round chandlo of kumkum on the forehead of Gunatitanand Swami.

Showing the tilak-chandlo to all, Bhagwan Swaminarayan stated, “This is our tilak. No God can compare with me and no sadhu can compare with this sadhu [Gunatitanand Swami].” 

In this manner, Maharaj revealed to all his own matchless identity as Purushottam and the identity of Gunatitanand Swami as his personified abode Aksharbrahma.

Reginald Heber, the then Lord Bishop of Calcutta, met Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

This meeting is considered to be a significant event in the history of the Swaminarayan Sampraday.

During their meeting, Bhagwan Swaminarayan explained his philosophy and teachings to Bishop Heber, and the two had a fruitful discussion. Bishop Heber was impressed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan's ideas and the devotion of his followers. See above some quotes from Bishop Heber's personal journal.

The meeting between Bishop Heber and Bhagwan Swaminarayan is remembered as a significant moment in the history of interfaith dialogue in India, as it brought together two leaders from different religions in a respectful and productive conversation.

179 years later in 2004, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj opened a 'Smruti Mandir' in Nadiad as a permanent memory of this historic meeting.

11 April 1911 
Chaitra sud 13, VS 1967
Bhagvati Diksha of Yogiji Maharaj in Vartal

Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj was born as Jhinabhai in the village of Dhari on 23 May 1892. 

His childhood was one of devotion par excellence along with samagam of the visiting sadhus from the Swaminarayan Mandir in Junagadh, including Sadguru Krishnacharan Swami.

It was under the guidance of Krishnacharan Swami that young Jhinabhai renounced home at the tender age of 16 with the blessings of his family. He joined the order of parshads in Junagadh in November 1908.

In Junagadh, young Jhina Bhagat served in various capacities as a parshad, winning the affection of the sadhus and devotees.

On the morning of 11 April 1911, 18-year-old Jhina Bhagat took bhagvati diksha into saffron at the hands of Acharya Shripatiprasadji Maharaj in Vartal.

On this auspicious occasion, Jhina Bhagat was renamed Sadhu Gnanjivandasji.

Due to his austere and devout nature, the sadhus and devotees fondly called him ‘Yogi’ or 'Jogi' while Krishnacharandas Swami called him ‘Gnanji Swami’.

He served as a sadhu in Junagadh Mandir for three months before taking a decision that turned out to be a pivotal development in the history of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

12 April 1951 
Chaitra Sud 6, VS 2007
Gadhada

To expound the pure principles of Akshar-Purushottam upasana as established by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj created five shikharbaddha mandirs: Bochasan, Sarangpur, Gondal, Atladra and Gadhada.

On the auspicious land of Gadhada which had been blessed with the 25-year-stay of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Shastriji Maharaj sought to acquire the land on the hill top on the banks of the sacred River Ghela. 

It was a colossal task, deemed impossible by many. Yet with faith in God and Guru, he persisted for 33 long years before finally acquiring the land in 1949.

Despite his advanced age and frail health, he meticulously oversaw the project of building a marble shikharbaddha mandir in Gadhada. 

During his final days in Sarangpur, despite being bedridden, he expressed a wish to travel to Gadhada. 

He travelled by car and reached Gadhada on the evening of 11 April 1951.

On the morning of 12 April 1951, he personally conducted the consecration of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta, bathing the murtis with sacred water from the River Ghela along with other pratishtha rituals.
After performing the arti, before preparing to return to Sarangpur, he exclaimed, "My vidhi is now over. Jogi Maharaj will come and complete the final consecration arti."

Six days following the passing of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta in the central shrine of the grand marble mandir on 16 May 1951.

19 April 1905 
Chaitri Purnima
Vartal
Akshar-Purushhottam Maharajni jay hailed by Galbhai.

While discussions about the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy did take place in some nooks and corners of Vartal and other mandirs of the Swaminarayan Sampraday, it was a knowledge not always easy to digest, despite its prevalence from the time of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. 

In April 1905, the Chaitra Punam festival would soon be celebrated in Vartal. Shastriji Maharaj was ill in Chansad at the time.

With Swamishri’s consent, Kalidasbhai and Galbhai of Chansad along with several other devotees set out for Vartal to attend the festival.

As soon as Acharya Maharaj arrived in the Punam assembly, Galbhai exclaimed, “Sahajanand Swami Maharajni Jay!” Everyone repeated the call. 

Immediately Galbhai followed, “Akshar-Purushottam Maharajni Jay!” 
Again, everyone repeated.

This was maybe the first time that this jay was extolled publicly at such a gathering.

Today, due to the efforts of the Gunatit Gurus, that same jaynaad glorying Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj is hailed at hundreds of mandirs and thousands of homes around the world.

Akshar-Purushottam Maharajni Jay!!!

It had been a struggle to complete the mandir, but Swamishri had ensured its completion through personally managing the project, which paid homage to the tremendous efforts of Shastriji Maharaj in propagating the eternal upasana of Akshar-Purushottam.

This Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir has been a witness to Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s guru-bhakti. Many have done darshan of his overflowing joy at doing darshan of his guru. Even when ill and frail in Sarangpur, he would regularly insist on going for darshan at the mandir.

Even on 17 August 2016, after he had reverted to Akshardham four days earlier, his divine body was taken to the smruti mandir for one last time.

Swamishri’s guru-bhakti was such that he had instructed years before that his final rites be performed at a location directly opposite this mandir so that Shastriji Maharaj’s drashti would remain upon him for eternity.

It was to be the first of many mandirs opened in East Africa with the blessings of Yogiji Maharaj, with mandirs later opening in Kampala (1960), Jinja (1960), Tororo (1960), Gulu (1966), and Nairobi (1970).

5 May 2013
Ahmedabad to Sarangpur

On that bright sunny morning in Ahmedabad, Bapa, you took us all by surprise! There were no special or specific programmes planned for that day. Yes, it was Sunday, so Sunday sabha in the evening at Shahibaug Mandir. Yes, it was Ekadashi, so a day of fasting. Nothing more.

The sadhus, parshads and sadhaks in Sarangpur were going about their various seva chores allocated to them as it was a Sunday, a day away from studies. No-one had any idea what would unfold later that day.

That morning, back in Ahmedabad, the one who had never insisted on anything for himself in his entire life unexpectedly insisted. 
'I want to go to Sarangpur!'
'OK Bapa, we can go in a couple of days once the arrangements are done'
'No, I want to go to Sarangpur. I want to go today!'

The rest is history.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj departed in the evening from Ahmedabad to reach Sarangpur. It was to be the beginning of a three-year long stay in Sarangpur. After decades of relentless vicharan, it was Swamishri’s inner wish to stay in Sarangpur for the final years of his life.

Despite being bedridden, his work continued unabated day and night around the world. 
He remained optimistic under the most trying of circumstances. 
He defied us with his resilience and astounded all with his ability to recover from any illness. 
No expectations and no complaints, he gave hope and continued to give darshan and bless countless sadhus and devotees.
His characteristic smile and laughter will continue to inspire us.
His legacy will remain forever...

5 May 2013 Ahmedabad to Sarangpur On that bright sunny morning in Ahmedabad, Bapa, you took us all by surprise! There were no special or specific programmes planned for that day. Yes, it was Sunday, so Sunday sabha in the evening at Shahibaug Mandir. Yes…

The day you arrived in Sarangpur, a place which you considered your home.

That small village in India became the centre of our universe for those years.

The joy was palpable that day in the hearts of all, and you even greeted your beloved Mahant Swami on that day.

You were used to travelling from village to village.

For example, in 1981, you visited over 450 villages.
In 1985, you visited over 344 places.
In 1990, you visited over 260 places.

From visiting multiple villages every single day, now, all of a sudden, you were in only one place.

But you were never disturbed. Only forever joyful.

You would personally meet hundreds of thousands. You were the ‘people’s guru’. Living your every second, of every day, amidst devotees.

And now you would spend most of your day in your room surrounded only by a handful of swamis.

But you were never lonely, never gloomy, never sorrowful. 

You always remained happy due to the bliss of God you forever experienced.

Never asking: ‘How are things running?’, ‘Is everything OK?, ‘Is the Akshardham we built in Delhi running okay?’, ‘Is the mandir we built in London still attracting visitors?’

No, not a single question. You trusted those you had guided, nurtured, and appointed.
You did everything, but never owned anything.
You built this entire global spiritual organisation from the ground up, but were attached to only God. 

From inspecting plans and examining stones, you were now waving chadis and throwing balls. But you were still joyful.

And yes, we will forever sing songs of your glory of those glorious days when you were an active and unstoppable force walking from house to house, and leading so many projects worldwide. 

But amazingly, we will also fondly remember these years when you were bound to a wheelchair.

Because you were our Bapa. Still the same smile, the same radiance, and the same inspiration.
Humility. As a teenager, Shastriji Maharaj had taught you to fold your hands, and in that same Sarangpur - 75 years later - until the very end, you kept your hands forever folded.

Those electric moments will stay with us forever. You brought an explosion of joy, energy, positivity, devotion, spirituality. Pure vibes.

You gave us darshan and bliss in so many ways. Obliging to every single request. Garlands, Hindolo, Rangotsav, Shakotsav, instruments - the list is endless. But you continued doing what you did your entire life - selflessly giving to others.

What was the secret of your bliss? 
When you were barely able to speak, and when you were frail, there was one thing which nobody could ever deny. 
Your everlasting devotion to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and your gurus. 

It was so deep, so entrenched into your very existence, it was who you were, at your very core. The conversations we see in the above videos reveal this so starkly.

And how can we ever forget your smile and laughter. It was divine. Infectious.

You were an epic human being. In fact, you were not a human being, you were the Satpurush, Aksharbrahma, Bhagwan-na akhand dharak sant. A being of a completely different realm. 

But at the same time, you were an adorable human - so loveable, so delightful, so magical, so innocent, so perfect. 

The ultimate combination of divinity and humanity.
And yes, there were so many divine moments where you also expressed your love for Pujya Mahant Swami...

Beauty. 
He was beautiful, but not like the way we talk of other humans in the world. 
He was beautiful for the way he thought. 
He was beautiful for the sparkle in his eyes when he talked about the Guru and God he loved. 
He was beautiful for his ability to make other people smile, even when he was frail and ill. 
No, he wasn't only beautiful for the radiance of his face. 
He was beautiful, deep down to his soul. 
He was beautiful and he was our guru. 
Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Bapa.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj, On this historic day of 5 May, we fondly remember you, Bapa. Today we reflect upon what you taught us in the final years you stayed amidst us on this earth.

During the Sarangpur Mandir Shatabdi Mahotsav, Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave a ‘kol’ to take all to Akshardham. This was to be the final time he gave such an ‘Akshardhamno kol’. 

All were witness to his unparalleled ishta-bhakti on this occasion as well. In every moment of his life, he put God forward. Age, circumstances, the scale of his achievements over all these decades, even the condition of his own body could massively change, but nothing could sway him from his ishta-bhakti. That remained unchanging, because that is who he was, at his core. The same ishta-bhakti he had throughout his life, was the same ishta-bhakti he had in the final year of his life, when his hands could barely move, but he'd still always reach out for his beloved Thakorji, because that devotion to God was never something he learnt or cultivated; it was who he was.

For many around the world, this ‘Akshardhamno kol’ is etched in our hearts as a permanent reminder of the everlasting peace that the Satpurush can grant. Despite the many challenges, hardships, and miseries life can bring, in such moments, the Satpurush can grant us with bliss. Such reassurances fill hearts with joy and security and make so many fearless in the face of death, disease, disappointment, and despair.

Gadhada Mandir Murti Pratishtha

In the town of Gadhpur sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan from 1805 to 1830, Shastriji Maharaj went to great efforts to fulfil Bhagwan Swaminarayan's sankalp of building a grand shikharbaddh mandir on the hillock on the banks of the River Ghela.

After 33 years of perseverance in trying to acquire the land, he eventually succeeded and performed the foundation stone laying ceremony in 1949. He began the construction of a marble mandir and shortly before the scheduled pratishtha, he visited Gadhada despite being bedridden with illness in Sarangpur. 

On 12 April 1951, he bathed the murtis with water from the sacred River Ghela and performed the pratishtha rituals, before proclaiming: "My vidhi is now over. Jogi will come and perform the [final pratishtha] arti."

Six days following the passing of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta in the central shrine of the grand marble mandir on 16 May 1951.

18 May 2001
Vaishakh vad 10, VS 2057
Sankari, India

Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated and performed the murti-pratishtha at the new BAPS mandir in Sankari.

Sankari is a very small village with a population of no more than a hundred people and a single street of homes. 

The first shikharbaddh mandir consecrated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in this village in 1971. 

Over the decades, the efforts of Swamishri and sadhus saw Satsang flourish in the region of Sankari. They travelled to the tribal villages and inspired thousands to give up addictions and superstitions. The Sankari mandir soon burgeoned into a centre for spiritual and moral regeneration. 

In 1988, a portion of the mandir land was transformed for over six months into an ideal cattle camp for the drought-stricken cattle. 

Every Punam, 6,000 to 7,000 devotees would come for darshan.

With the growing magnitude of Satsang, the need for a larger mandir complex became necessary. To satisfy the increasing needs, Swamishri performed the ground-breaking ceremony for a new shikharbaddh mandir on 15 January 1996. Within 5 years, the intricately carved mandir made of pink sandstone was ready.

The inauguration ceremony of the newly built mandir was performed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj on 18 May 2001.

22 to 28 May 1951
Anand
Beginning of a new era: Vinubhai meets Yogiji Maharaj

It was not long after Shastriji Maharaj's passing in Sarangpur on 10 May 1951.

Six days later, Yogiji Maharaj completed the murti-pratishtha in Gadhada. 

On 19 May, rituals to mark the 17th Patotsav of Gondal Mandir were held in the presence of numerous devotees from East Africa.

After celebrating Vaishakhi Punam in Gondal, Yogiji Maharaj travelled to the region of Charotar, where he visited many villages and graced the village homes of many of those devotees who had now settled in East Africa. 

It was during this time that Yogiji Maharaj stayed for six days in Anand and visited the home of Manilal Naranbhai Patel, whose young son came in touch with Yogiji Maharaj for the very first time.

It was a life-changing spiritual experience for the 17-year-old Vinubhai. Soon after this, he was so moved by the saintliness of Yogiji Maharaj, that he longed to spend every spare moment in his guru's company.

From 1951 to 1957, young Vinubhai often rushed to Yogiji Maharaj during his vacations. He was totally won over by Yogiji Maharaj’s selfless love, and he was determined to offer his all at the feet of Yogiji Maharaj.

This eventually culminated in Yogiji Maharaj ordaining Vinubhai as a parshad in February 1957.

30 May 1950
Anand, Gujarat, India

Sadguru Nirgundas Swami passes away to Akshardham

Nirgundas Swami was a pioneer in the history of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. He surrendered his genius, personality and standing at the feet of Shastriji Maharaj, who he humbly served until his last breath. 

In a letter dated 28 July 1949 to the politician Gulzarilal Nanda, Nirgundas Swami proclaims, “Shastriji Maharaj was never influenced by anyone and was able to control such free-willed people as me.” 

Moreover, he wrote in his personal journal: “No one had the courage to tell me to wear saffron [to become a sadhu], but Shastriji Maharaj did. He told me that my intellect, knowledge, and ability would shine more in saffron than in white. These words touched me and I became a sadhu.”

Such was Nirgundas Swami’s respect for Shastriji Maharaj, he would carry out any command given by his guru to earn his rajipo.

Inspired by Gunatitanand Swami’s vision of Satsang being spread to all corners of the Earth and by Shastriji Maharaj’s words, Nirgundas Swami began writing of the greatness of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and Shastriji Maharaj in a stream of letters to Africa, where Harmanbhai and Maganbhai, two devotees, had established Satsang. Nirgundas Swami’s letters were not just a few pages long, but were sometimes up to a hundred pages in length! Moreover, his letters were organised, well-written, point-to-point, clear, and faithful to the principles of the Vachanamrut and other scriptures of the Sampraday.

Shastriji Maharaj would often speak of the pivotal role played by Nirgundas Swami in propagating the Akshar-Purushottam upasana through vicharan, letters and katha.

🎵 Mārā Bochāsaṇnā belī, vahālā Akṣhar Puruṣhottam

Today is World Environment Day, a moment to reflect not just on the state of our planet, but on the lives of those who honour it every single day through their actions, their choices, and their love. 

One such person is our very own guru, Mahant Swami Maharaj.

From the very beginning, Mahant Swami Maharaj’s bond with nature has been intimate and reverent. As a young man, he studied agriculture. In every major festival of BAPS, he was given the responsibility of landscaping. While others may see trees and nature as decoration, he saw them as something to revere and care for. He would plant each sapling with care and even talk to the plants. He would address them as muktas. This has been seen by many eyewitnesses of his seva. He would speak to the plants and lovingly encourage them to grow. Science today tells us that such words, such intention, can help plants thrive.

As the spiritual leader of BAPS, Mahant Swami Maharaj continues to inspire and guide countless environmental initiatives around the world. From promoting sustainable temple construction to initiating large-scale water relief projects during droughts, and championing recycling and waste reduction efforts, his vision extends across the global BAPS community. Yet these actions are not mere compliance with modern trends; they flow from his own deep ethic of respect, responsibility, and harmony with nature.

Even now, at 91, his care for the environment is lived out in the smallest of gestures. 
- He never lets the tap run when brushing his teeth, he fills a small vessel and uses only what is needed. 
- Just last month, he waited patiently for an ant to climb out of a sink before letting the water flow. 
- Earlier this year in Melbourne, a few horses were grazing outside his residence. He had been resting, but upon waking, his very first question was whether the horses had been fed and cared for. 

At 91. Imagine, then, the decades before, how many animals he must have noticed, how many trees he must have planted, how many small, unseen acts of compassion he must have carried out. 
For Mahant Swami Maharaj, to love God is to love all that God has made.

18 June 1800 
Jeth vad 12 
Piplana, India 

Following his 7-year van vicharan and 10 long months in Loj, 19-year-old Nilkanth Varni first meets Guru Ramanand Swami in the village of Piplana on 18 June 1800.

Ramanand Swami repeated what he had been saying for many years: “I am only a drumbeater, but the real actor is this brahmachari Nilkanth.”

Four months later, in Piplana, on 28 October 1800 (Kartak sud 11), he gave bhagvati diksha to Nilkanth and named him Sahajanand Swami and Narayanmuni.

Nishkulanand Swami describes this meeting in Piplana in prakran 44 of the Bhaktachintamani:

Param hitkārī bahunāmī, dīṭhā sinhāsan par swāmī. 25
Tene dekhīne pāmyā ānand, tyāre uṭhyā Swāmī Rāmānand;
Karyā Nīlkanṭhe danḍavat, tene uṭhāḍyā swāmīe tarat. 26
Preme maḷīne besāryā pās, karī bījānī bahu āsavās;
Jevā kahyātā sādhue maḷī, tevā dīṭhā chhe Varṇīe vaḷī. 27
Pāmyā paramānand sukh bhārī, āvyā harṣhanā nayaṇe vāri;
Thayā brahmachārī romānchite, joī rahyā sāmu bahu prītye. 28
Tem joī rahyā swāmī hete, ek mīṭe maṭakā rahite;

29 June 1792 
Ashadh sud 10
Ayodhya, India

🌄 Long before sunrise on that Friday morning in Ayodhya, while the whole town was sunk in sleep, Ghanshyam was wide awake. He had resolved to leave the comforts of his home and embrace the hardships of a yogi. The dark, rainy night didn't dampen his spirit. 

📿 Barefoot and barebodied, wearing only a loin cloth, he carried a gourd and palash stick; a rosary, shaligram, and a short summary of the scriptures remained his only possessions. 

🌎 Ghanshyam renounced his family to make the whole world his family; to enlighten and elevate everyone he met along his journey of redemption. This moment of renunciation was historic.

25 July 1829
Gadhada, India

Selected discourses of Bhagwan Swaminarayan delivered between 1819 and 1829 have been compiled in the Vachanamrut, which contains a total of 273 discourses.

Narrated on 25 July 1829, the last recorded Vachanamrut was 'Gadhada III 39: Vishalyakaraṇī Aushadhinu'.

In the conclusion of this final Vachanamrut, Bhagwan Swaminarayan says:
▪️"It is the principle of all of the scriptures that one should eradicate māyā and develop love for God."
▪️ “A devotee of God requires the strength of two things: ātmā-realization and the greatness of God."
▪️"I deliver these discourses to you not from any imagination of my mind, nor to display any sort of aptitude. I have experienced all that I have spoken about. In fact, I speak in accordance to what I practice."

It was also the final Vachanamrut that was read to Yogiji Maharaj. On the early morning of 16 January 1971, a week before he passed away to Akshardham, Yogiji Maharaj asked for the Vachanamrut to be read. The sevak read this Vachanamut. After this, until his passing, Yogiji Maharaj was not able to listen to the Vachanamrut again.

Adhik Shravan Vad 5, VS 2041 
Alexandra Park, London

20 July 1985 became a part of BAPS history as Queens Park Rangers Stadium witnessed the first ever Suvarna Mahotsav held to honour Pramukh Swami Maharaj. 

The volunteers had worked hard for several months in planning and setting up the festival, and for them this was going to be the ultimate experience.

However, at Swamishri’s wish, they stayed at the Cultural Festival of India grounds at Alexandra Park to run the exhibitions, food stalls, and other departments. 

The moment of supreme joy arrived at QPR Stadium. Swamishri had been honoured and thousands cheered his name and echoed cries of jubilation.

When the celebrations were over, a sadhu asked Swamishri, “What were you thinking while being weighed?” “I was thinking about the yuvaks who were doing seva back at Ally Pally.”

Swamishri’s response was instant and thought-provoking. It is impossible to think of others while one is being showered with such honour and praise.

A few days later, on 5 August, Swamishri, out of sheer compassion, arranged for a special festival for the volunteers.

The vibrations from the voices of the sadhus and parshads singing could be felt in each and every person's heart, as Swamishri plucked people from the crowd to join in a dance at the end of the special Suvarna Mahotsav programme arranged exclusively for the volunteers.

The few precious seconds previously witnessed at QPR Stadium when Swamishri had danced before departing, were brought back again. This time, his beloved volunteers were much closer and, for them, Swamishri danced a little longer. 

Unbelievable scenes of jubilation, unimaginable atmosphere and bliss... 

This was how Swamishri rewarded those volunteers who had stayed back to serve at the CFI grounds at Alexandra Park.

Bapa,
 
Today was a day we want to forget but that we never will.
Heartache, wrenching pain, and an endless flow of tears.
Wails of pain, anguish and sorrow heard in every corner. 
Grief is the price of love is what we realised on that fateful day.

Today, we were all the same. 
Age, gender, nationality, sadhu, householder - nothing mattered.
We were sat, for hours, in the scorching heat, as one family. 
Your family.
You had said 'BAPS Ek Parivar' many times, but on that day, we felt it like never before.
Our hearts and minds united by our love, and grief, for you.

Today, we welcomed you for the final time.
For decades, your arrivals were always the most memorable. Moments that filled our hearts with elation. Today, however, our hearts were empty. Void. Numb.
You taught us to perform bhakti and adorned our lives with puja, thal, arti.
Today was the last arti we would offer to you.

Today, we would see your mesmerising face for the last time.
Your beautiful, innocent face would light up our lives with joy.
But today was different. There was only pain.
The final time this earth was graced with the presence of your body... 
The smile that mesmerises millions...
The arms that helped thousands...
The hands that blessed countless...
The legs that walked from house to house...
All to give to joy to others.

Today, a day we would never imagine.
You were invincible. You were the Bapa that would always be there.
You were the Bapa we were born with. Bapa that was always a ‘given' in life.
For those four days you were still before our eyes, with us.
But today, you - the almighty, the powerful, the Bapa that would be there forever - were suddenly engulfed by flames.

Today, we realised how deep your devotion was.
Guru and God were the focus throughout your life.
In your final seconds, you had your beloved Thakorji on your chest.
And the murti of your guru in your presence.
Today, even after you have breathed your last, your devotion remains eternal.

18 August 1897

Bhagatji Maharaj welcomed with a grand reception at Junagadh

Since his exile from the Satsang - imposed by the authorities in Vadtal for propagating the glory of Gunatitanand Swami - Bhagatji Maharaj had not visited Junagadh. 

Over 30 years had passed, yet Bhagatji Maharaj did not go to Junagadh due to opposition and the absence of Acharya Maharaj’s orders. Shastri Yagnapurushdasji, however, decided to accord a grand reception to Bhagatji at the very place where he had been insulted.

In VS 1953 (1897 CE), he persuaded Acharya Viharilalji Maharaj to invite Bhagatji on the occasion of the Janmashtami festival to be celebrated in Junagadh.

Bhagatji Maharaj arrived in Junagadh two days prior to the festival. He was received along with Acharya Maharaj at Junagadh railway station with traditional fanfare. Like Acharya Maharaj, Bhagatji Maharaj and his disciples were driven in a decorated carriage. Special arrangements were made at the mandir to make their stay comfortable. Yagnapurushdasji was assisted by Kothari Jibhai of Junagadh in making these arrangements for Bhagatji.

The news of Bhagatji’s arrival in Junagadh spread all over the city. All the Nagar devotees came to the mandir for Bhagatji’s darshan. Here, he met senior sadhus such as Balmukunddasji and Jaga Bhagat, who had sincerely served Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami. For many days, these great stalwarts of the Gunatit Gnan came together to engage in discourses and scriptural discussions to extol the glory of Akshar and Purushottam.

Bhagatji's disciples had sponsored the meals on the day after Janmashtami at Junagadh Mandir where he served the sadhus and devotees most affectionately.

text:
Happy 30th Birthday to London Mandir! 

🛕 How and why did Pramukh Swami Maharaj gift us the very first traditional Hindu mandir in the Western world right here in London?

✨ On this historic and heartfelt occasion, let us pause and remember our beloved guru.

📜 Mahant Swami Maharaj has given us all agna to reflect daily on prapti. Reading this short article can help us consolidate our understanding of prapti, because it is more than just revisiting history; it is a chance to introspect and awaken once more to the glory of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

21 August 1799 
Shravan vad 6 
Loj, India

After his epic 2,610 days (7 years, 1 month and 24 days) of pilgrimage throughout India, covering over 12,000 kilometres, Nilkanth Varni arrived in Loj.

Nilkanth bathed in the stepwell and retired into a meditative posture beneath a sprawling banyan tree nearby. 

Sukhanand Swami from Ramanand Swami’s ashram came to fill his pot from the stepwell.

Upon seeing the gentle, teenage yogi, he, too, was mesmerised. He came and stood before Nilkanth, waiting for him to open his eyes.

Sukhanand Swami asked: “Brahmachariji, where do you come from? What is your name? Who are your parents? Why have you renounced your home? And who is your guru?” 

 “Sadhuram! A renunciant has no caste, country or relatives. One who redeems from worldly bondage is a true parent or guru! I am in search of such a guru,” Nilkanth replied softly.

Nilkanth Varni then proceeded to the ashram in Loj to meet Muktanand Swami. Nilkanth revealed to Muktanand Swami: “My mind is at peace in your ashram. The sadhus here are of a peaceful disposition.” 

“You may ask freely whatever questions you have,” Muktanand Swami requested.

Nilkanth then posed the five questions he had been asking throughout his travels. Muktanand Swami satisfactorily elaborated upon the natures of jiva, ishwar, maya, Brahma and Parabrahma. Nilkanth was satisfied with the answers and decided to stay at the ashram for the darshan of guru Ramanand Swami.

Jhina Bhagat (Yogiji Maharaj) met Shastriji Maharaj for the first time.

In August 1910, Shastriji Maharaj arrived in Rajkot, where he stayed at the house of Krishnaji Ada. 

Some sadhus and parshads from Junagadh were also in vicharan in Rajkot at the time. When Jhina Bhagat of Junagadh heard this news of Shastriji Maharaj, he felt a strong desire to have the darshan of Shastriji Maharaj, as he had often heard of the glory of Shastriji Maharaj from various sadhus and devotees in Junagadh.

So, early in the morning, under the pretext of going for a bath in the River Aji, Jhina Bhagat and three other sadhus proceeded to the house of Krishnaji Ada.

When Shastriji Maharaj awoke, Jadavjibhai informed him that some sadhus had come for darshan. Shastriji Maharaj went to the room where the sadhus were waiting. 

Jhina Bhagat and the other sadhus paid reverence to Shastriji Maharaj before presenting to him a sanctified mala and tumbdi, which had been used by Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami. Shastriji Maharaj was greatly pleased.

Jhina Bhagat could not take his eyes off Shastriji Maharaj and looked at him with great reverence. Shastriji Maharaj, too, looked at Jhina Bhagat with much affection.

From that day, Jhina Bhagat mentally accepted Shastriji Maharaj as his guru.

After receiving bhagvati diksha on 11 April 1911, when he was named Gnanjivandas Swami, Yogiji Maharaj left Junagadh on 9 July 1911 to join Shastriji Maharaj in his noble mission of propagating the Akshar-Purushottam upasana.

Prasang on Swamishri's devotion:
Following his cataract operation, Pramukh Swami was recovering in a room at the Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary. His eyes were bandaged shut and so he called out and asked as to who was present. A local youth was sitting in the room and asked Swami what he needed. Since it was the evening, Swami asked him to recite the cheshta. The youth replied, “I don’t know the cheshta.” So Swami instructed him to read it from a kirtan book, which he did not have. 8 September 1981
Mumbai, India 

Cholecystectomy operation to remove gall bladder performed on Pramukh Swami Maharaj at Cumballa Hill Hospital, Mumbai, by Dr A.R. Patel. 

The gall bladder was removed due to multiple gallstones and had been causing health issues for some time. Despite the difficulties, Swamishri's vicharan had continued unabated, and he had resisted doctors' recommendations to have the surgery done in 1980, instead preferring to wait until the bicentenary celebrations of Bhagwan Swaminarayan were complete.

It was a major operation in those days - nowadays it can be simply removed by keyhole laparoscopic surgery - requiring many days in hospital post-operation. After resting and recuperating in Mumbai, Swamishri resumed his vicharan.

Soon after the gall bladder operation, Swamishri was in Gondal. 

One day, after Swamishri took breakfast, a balak named Chandrakant came rushing. He asked Swamishri in childish prattle, “Bapa, where is your operation scar?” He had once heard his parents talking about the operation.

The devotees who saw the child were quite surprised with the balak's request. Swamishri, however, casually lifted his upper cloth (gatariyu) and showed him the scar. He said to the balak, “Here, run your hand on it so that it heals soon.” Innocently, Chandrakant ran his hand on the scar. Swamishri then remarked, “Now it will heal quickly."

Such was Swamishri's affectionate nature.

This remarkable painting, created in 1860, is now 165 years old and stands as one of the earliest known visual representations of Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj. At the time, he was around 75 years old, radiating divine serenity and spiritual strength —qualities beautifully captured in this historic artwork. 

What makes this painting even more extraordinary is that it is currently the only known and most accurate depiction of Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj. It not only preserves his physical appearance, but also serves as a timeless tribute to his profound wisdom, selfless service, and eternal presence as Akshar, the divine abode of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. 

This sacred image continues to inspire generations of devotees, offering a rare and invaluable glimpse into the divine past.

28 September 1784

Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami is born as Mulji Sharma in Bhadra on the auspicious day of Sharad Purnima. 

Gunatitanand Swami was the first spiritual successor of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. He was revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan to be Aksharbrahma, the perfectly enlightened ideal devotee and the closest entity to God, glorified in the Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagwad Gita, and many other Hindu shastras. 

Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami extolled Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s true glory as Parabrahma Purushottam Narayan through his profound saintliness, matchless wisdom, inspiring discourses, and constant communion with God. His discipline, devotion, and service were exemplary, inspiring all who came into his contact. 

As Aksharbrahma, he forever remains manifest on Earth as the enlightened guru, helping aspirants attain moksha.

A short letter from guru Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj is all it took for him to let go of his life. Today, the world knows him as Pramukh Swami Maharaj. It is a day we reflect on his tyag.

Tyaga is renunciation: letting go of those things that hinder one’s quest for moksha. The Upanishads explain the importance of tyaga: “One who wants to attain God must let go of all worldly attachments.”

The ultimate form of tyaga is not just letting go, but also selflessly sacrificing one’s self for the benefit of humankind. He left his home, his relatives, his ambitions and those dear to him to selflessly give his all for God, guru, and humanity. Until his very last breath, Swamishri lived by the sentiments with which he renounced: devotion and selfless service. The Kaivalya Upanishad states, “Immortality cannot be achieved by wealth, power or good deeds. It can only be achieved by tyag.” Pramukh Swami Maharaj is immortal.

He left his home to make the world his home.
He left his family to make all of humanity his family.

It was a sad day in many ways, but significant and life-changing nevertheless. 

Having been ordained as a sadhu at the age of 17 in November 1882, Shastriji Maharaj had spent almost 23 years in Vartal as a sadhu, where his unmatched saintliness and penetrating discourses inspired many.

Despite the overwhelming odds and insurmountable challenges, through his sheer determination, unparalleled dedication, and deep faith, he would go on to establish Akshar-Purushottam mandirs in Bochasan, Sarangpur, Gondal, Atladra, and Gadhada over the following 45 years.

Monday 16 November 1801 
(Kartak sud 11, AS 1858) 
Jetpur, India

Sahajanand Swami is appointed the leader of the Sampraday by Ramanand Swami

Early morning, before the pre-dawn hours, Ramanand Swami arranged a ritual bath for Sahajanand Swami by the River Bhadar Ganga. The brahmins chanted mantras and Ramanand Swami, Muktanand Swami and others performed the 16 rituals of worship of Sahajanand Swami. Thereafter, Sahajanand Swami put on a pair of new clothes, and after completing his daily puja rituals, went with Ramanand Swami to the assembly hall. Sahajanand Swami and Ramanand Swami sat before the yagna fire and performed the rituals. 

Ramanand Swami then led the 20-year-old Sahajanand Swami to a decorative, high seat and officially appointed him as his successor and head of the Fellowship. The assembly hailed the name of Sahajanand Swami with thunderous applause. 

Ramanand Swami said to Sahajanand Swami: “Swami, I am very happy with you for suppressing your spirit of renunciation to accept this seat at my word. I do not know what to give to you because you are the supreme master and the all-doer. But still I feel that I should give something as a gift to you. Pray, tell me what should I offer you.” 

Sahajanand Swami prostrated in veneration to Guru Ramanand Swami and humbly declared, “You are my guru. Out of love and reverence, you have appointed me as the head. On this occasion I would like you to bless me with two boons.” 

“Swami, my heart shudders at the miseries of devotees. Therefore, if your devotee is to suffer the pain of a scorpion bite, then let that pain come to me multiplied millions of times in every pore of my body instead. 

Secondly, if your devotee is fated to have the begging bowl, then let the begging bowl come to me instead; but never may your devotee be miserable because of food and clothes. I ask you to grant me these two boons." 

Ramanand Swami then called Mulji Sharma of Bhadra on stage and introduced him to Sahajanand Swami. The latter responded, “Mulji is my abode, Akshardham. In the future, he will be ordained as a sadhu and be named as Gunatitanand Swami.”

21 November 1809
(Kartik sud Punam, Samvat 1866)
Mulji Sharma renounces Bhadra.
"Brahma tej sukay chhe. Ghar baline aviya chho?" 

In Bhadra, Mulji Bhakta was busy diverting water to his sugarcane field situated by the riverbank. He was thinking about when Shriji Maharaj would instruct him to renounce this world. 

Suddenly, he had a vision of Shriji Maharaj in the sky. Maharaj was wearing a yellow pitambar and a southern-style pagh. 

Maharaj said to Mulji Bhakta, “What have you come for and what are you doing? The divine light of Brahma has faded away from the world, so leave now.” 

Without a moment’s delay, Mulji left his work. He did not even go home, but headed straight to Gadhada to meet Maharaj. After that, Mulji requested Shri Hari to allow him to remain in his service. 

Mulji had detached himself completely from the world and had no interest whatsoever in material objects. In order that others may realise the spiritual state of Mulji, Shriji Maharaj tested him and said, “I will make you a sadhu, but have you burnt your house or have you kept it intact?” 

The simple-natured Mulji replied, “Maharaj, the house is as it is.” 

“Then go and burn it, and come back. I’ll make you a sadhu after that,” instructed Maharaj. 

To fulfil Maharaj’s order, Mulji left immediately for Bhadra. Maharaj knew that Mulji would come back only after burning his house. So he immediately sent Bhaguji and called him back. From the spiritual viewpoint, Mulji had already burnt all ties of affection with his family, estate, and relatives from his heart. But he was also prepared to destroy all the physical ties. Seeing his profound detachment, Maharaj showered praise on him.

A short while later in Dabhan on 20 January 1810, Mulji was ordained as a sadhu by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and renamed Gunatitanand Swami. On that day, Bhagwan Swaminarayan revealed the glory of Gunatitanand Swami as Aksharbrahma, his divine abode.

The 6,600 hand-carved motifs depict a mosaic of tales of inspiration, devotion and dedication, along with historical figures from Hindu Dharma. Artisans created the carvings in India with great love, skill, and patience before the pieces were shipped to Chino Hills. 

The Mandir is situated on a 20-acre site, complete with a 91-foot lotus-shaped reflection pond, a cultural centre, gymnasium, and classrooms.

As the first earthquake-proof mandir in the world, the upper structure of the complex is protected from earthquake damage by separating it from the base with a series of 40 base-isolator units. 

The Mandir also uses a solar power system to generate electricity and reduce adverse effects on the environment. The Mandir combines the best of traditional stone art and architecture and the best of modern technology.

With these words, he touched his [raas] stick on Gunatitanand Swami’s chest and said, ‘Jugo jug jivo evã jogi, jugo jug jivo evã jogiyã.’ So saying, Shriji Maharaj himself first proclaimed the glory of [Gunatitanand] Swami."

4 March 1809
Sarangpur, India

On 4 March 1809, Bhagwan Swaminarayan rode his horse, Rojho, upon the land of Sarangpur and declared, "Today, we have laid the foundation for a great mandir here."

In 1825, he reaffirmed this divine promise to Jiva Khachar and the devotees of Sarangpur: "A grand mandir will rise on this very spot we have chosen. I shall reside here along with my Dham and muktas, and this Dham will become world-renowned."

Bhagwan Swaminarayan entered the village on horseback with the sadhus, with of all of them singing. Maharaj then made a circle with his stallion, Rojho. 

The devotees asked Maharaj: ‘Why did you make a circle with your horse?’

Maharaj then said:
Shriji kahe suno tame dās – Rame Hari rangatāli…
Asur āptā tamne trās – Rame Hari…
Tethi karyu asur nighan – Rame; Have sukh raho harijan – Rame Hari…
Vali ghodo unmatt behad – Rame; Tethi haran karyo teno mada – Rame Hari…
Vali kundāni jāno vāt – Rame; Karyu motā mandirnu khāt – Rame Hari…
Dhām sahit raheshu ame āhi – Rame; Evu mandir thāshe sukhdāi – Rame Hari…
Āj thaki vite varas shat – Rame. Thāshe motu mandir trat – Rame Hari…
Suni Harinā agam vachan – Rame. Thayā rāji puranā harijan – Rame Hari…

Also, this stallion who is arrogant, has now become tamed.
Now come to know the reason behind this circle; I have performed the ground-breaking ceremony of a grand mandir.
I will reside here with my abode [choicest devotee]; such a magnificent mandir will stand here.

A hundred years from today, a large mandir will be duly built.
Hearing Shri Hari’s premonition, the devotees of Sarangpur were delighted.

Fast forward 100 years...

Around 1910, shortly after the opening of the mandir in Bochasan in 1907, Shastriji Maharaj – on his way to the large kund to bathe – stopped at the place where the mandir is currently situated.

Accompanied by one sadhu and Motibhai, Swamishri said to Motibhai, “Motibhai! Shriji Maharaj had stopped here and circled around on his Rojho horse at this location and declared, ‘I am today performing the groundbreaking ceremony of a large mandir here.’ Therefore, a mandir will definitely be situated here.” With these words, Swamishri proceeded to bathe.

Some time later, Swamishri took a surveyor to the southern part of the village of Sarangpur to the place where Shriji Maharaj had encircled on his Rojho horse and proclaimed that he was performing the ground-breaking ceremony for a large mandir. Swamishri put in a request for all of this sanctified land. The surveyor soon mapped out the land and marked it out with pegs.

It was at this place where Shastriji Maharaj started building a mandir in Sarangpur.

After many moments of struggle and despite the unprecedented challenges, Shastriji Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha of Sarangpur Mandir on 8 May 1916.

He gave all the sadhus a small piece of yellow clay sourced from a local pond. The following morning, Bhagwan Swaminarayan did not see a tilak on any foreheads. After further inquiry, he found that the sadhus had consumed the clay, thinking it to be prasad. He distributed another piece and instructed them to perform a tilak.

The next day, he saw that the sadhus had applied tilaks of different shapes and sizes.

Bhagwan Swaminarayan then requested Gunatitanand Swami to come forward. With his own hands, Bhagwan Swaminarayan applied a clay tilak and a round chandlo of kumkum on the forehead of Gunatitanand Swami.

Showing the tilak-chandlo to all, Bhagwan Swaminarayan stated, “This is our tilak. No God can compare with me and no sadhu can compare with this sadhu [Gunatitanand Swami].” By pronouncing Gunatitanand Swami as his 'tilak', Bhagwan Swaminarayan was revealing the identity of his first spiritual successor.

In this manner, Maharaj revealed to all his own matchless identity as Purushottam and the identity of Gunatitanand Swami as his personified abode Aksharbrahma.

31 March 1960
Zambia

One Way! Road Closed!

On the evening of 31 March 1960, Yogiji Maharaj set out for Broken Hill in Rajnibhai’s car. At one point along the journey, there was a diversion sign and the road had been blocked with bitumen drums. However, Rajnibhai got out of the car, moved them aside, and proceeded along that route.

Swamishri asked him, "Guru! Why did you get down?"
"Bapa! These people often keep the drums in place and the road closed even after repairs are complete. That is why I got down to move them," replied Rajnibhai.

Swamishri remarked, "That wouldn't be the case; they would only keep it closed if the road is indeed closed! We should take the car down the diversion."

However, Rajnibhai insisted, "Bapa! There won’t be any trouble. We should continue along this main road." Swamishri did not press the matter further.

After travelling about a mile, the car encountered a broken section of the road. It was now impossible to proceed. The road was narrow and elevated above the surrounding land, making it impossible to even turn the car around. Nor could the vehicle be driven off the road. They were forced to reverse the car.

Swamishri asked, "What's happened?"
"Bapa! We cannot go forward, and there is no room to turn the car back."
Swamishri burst into laughter and, raising one hand with a characteristic gesture of his finger, said, "One way! Road closed!"
He then added, "Likewise, for Akshardham, it is one-way! The roads are closed! One must never perceive flaws or shortcomings in others; one must only see their virtues. The path is closed for those who perceive flaws. Seeing virtues is the only way!"

It was somewhat late by the time they reached Broken Hill. They stayed at Lallubhai’s residence and held a sabha. Devotees and well-wishers from several villages in the Kheda region participated and benefited on that occasion.

(Yogiji Maharaj Jivan Chaitra Part 3/69)

Bhagvati Diksha of Yogiji Maharaj in Vartal

Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj was born as Jhinabhai in the village of Dhari on 23 May 1892. 

His childhood was one of devotion par excellence along with samagam of the visiting sadhus from the Swaminarayan Mandir in Junagadh, including Sadguru Krishnacharan Swami.

It was under the guidance of Krishnacharan Swami that young Jhinabhai renounced home at the tender age of 16 with the blessings of his family. He joined the order of parshads in Junagadh in November 1908.

In Junagadh, young Jhina Bhagat served in various capacities as a parshad, winning the affection of the sadhus and devotees.

On the morning of 11 April 1911, 18-year-old Jhina Bhagat took bhagvati diksha into saffron at the hands of Acharya Shripatiprasadji Maharaj in Vartal.

On this auspicious occasion, Jhina Bhagat was renamed Sadhu Gnanjivandasji.

Due to his austere and devout nature, the sadhus and devotees fondly called him ‘Yogi’ or 'Jogi' while Krishnacharandas Swami called him ‘Gnanji Swami’.

He served as a sadhu in Junagadh Mandir for three months before taking a decision that turned out to be a pivotal development in the history of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

75 years ago today

Thursday 12 April 1951
Chaitra Sud 6, VS 2007
Gadhada

To expound the pure principles of Akshar-Purushottam upasana as revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj created five shikharbaddha mandirs: Bochasan, Sarangpur, Gondal, Atladara, and Gadhada.

On the auspicious land of Gadhada, which had been blessed with the 25-year-stay of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Shastriji Maharaj sought to acquire the land on the hilltop on the banks of the sacred River Ghela. 

It was a colossal task, deemed impossible by many. Yet with faith in God and Guru, he persisted for 33 long years before finally acquiring the land in 1949.

Despite his advanced age and frail health, he meticulously oversaw the project of building a marble shikharbaddha mandir in Gadhada. 

During his final days in Sarangpur, despite being bedridden, he expressed a wish to travel to Gadhada. 

He travelled by car and reached Gadhada on the evening of 11 April 1951.

On the morning of 12 April 1951, he personally consecrated the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta, bathing them with sacred water from the River Ghela along with other pratishtha rituals.

After performing the arti, before preparing to return to Sarangpur, he exclaimed, "My vidhi is now over. Jogi Maharaj will come and complete the final consecration arti."

Six days following the passing of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta in the central shrine of the grand marble mandir on 16 May 1951.

While discussions about the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy did take place in some nooks and corners of Vartal and other mandirs of the Swaminarayan Sampraday, it was a knowledge not always easy to digest, despite its prevalence from the time of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. 

In April 1905, the Chaitra Punam festival would soon be celebrated in Vartal. Shastriji Maharaj was ill in Chansad at the time.

With Swamishri’s consent, Kalidasbhai and Galbhai of Chansad along with several other devotees set out for Vartal to attend the festival.

As soon as Acharya Maharaj arrived in the Punam assembly, Galbhai exclaimed, “Sahajanand Swami Maharajni Jay!” Everyone repeated the call. 

Immediately Galbhai followed, “Akshar-Purushottam Maharajni Jay!” 
Again, everyone repeated.

This was maybe the first time that this jay was extolled publicly at such a gathering.

Today, due to the efforts of the Gunatit Gurus, that same jaynaad glorying Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj is hailed at hundreds of mandirs and thousands of homes around the world.

Shastriji Maharaj’s final rites had been conducted here on 11 May 1951, one day after his passing to Akshardham.

A smaller shrine had been constructed at this spot and opened by Yogiji Maharaj in 1952. But it had always been Yogiji Maharaj’s and Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s wish to construct a proper structure in eternal memory of their beloved guru.

It had been a struggle to complete the mandir, but Swamishri had ensured its completion through personally managing the project, which paid homage to the tremendous efforts of Shastriji Maharaj in propagating the eternal upasana of Akshar-Purushottam.

This Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir has been a witness to Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s guru-bhakti. Many have done darshan of his overflowing joy at doing darshan of his guru. Even when ill and frail in Sarangpur, he would regularly insist on going for darshan at the mandir.

On 17 August 2016, after he had reverted to Akshardham four days earlier, his divine body was taken to the smruti mandir for one last time.

Swamishri’s guru-bhakti was such that he had instructed years before that his final rites be performed at a location directly opposite this mandir so that Shastriji Maharaj’s drashti would remain upon him for eternity.

5 May 2013
Ahmedabad to Sarangpur

On that bright sunny morning in Ahmedabad, Bapa, you took us all by surprise! There were no special or specific programmes planned for that day. Yes, it was Sunday, so Sunday sabha in the evening at Shahibaug Mandir. Yes, it was Ekadashi, so a day of fasting. Nothing more.

The sadhus, parshads and sadhaks in Sarangpur were going about their various seva chores allocated to them as it was a Sunday, a day away from studies. No one had any idea what would unfold later that day.

That morning, back in Ahmedabad, the one who had never insisted on anything for himself in his entire life unexpectedly insisted. 
"I want to go to Sarangpur!" 
"OK Bapa, we can go in a couple of days once the arrangements are made." 
"No, I want to go to Sarangpur. I want to go today!" 

The rest is history.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj departed in the evening from Ahmedabad to reach Sarangpur. It was to be the beginning of a three-year long stay in Sarangpur. After decades of relentless vicharan, it was Swamishri’s inner wish to stay in Sarangpur for the final years of his life.

Despite being bedridden, his work continued unabated day and night around the world. 
He remained optimistic under the most trying of circumstances. 
He defied us with his resilience and astounded all with his ability to recover from any illness. 
No expectations and no complaints, he gave hope and continued to give darshan and bless countless sadhus and devotees.
His characteristic smile and laughter will continue to inspire us.
His legacy will remain forever... 

From 5 May 2013, Swamishri's vicharan until 13 August 2016 as below:
Sarangpur: 5 May 2013 to 1 August 2014 (453 days)
Gandhinagar: 1 August 2014 to 5 August 2014 (4 days)
Robbinsville: 5 August 2014 to 19 August 2014 (14 days)
Ahmedabad: 19 August 2014 to 25 August 2014 (6 days)
Sarangpur: 25 August 2014 to 13 August 2016 (719 days)

The siren's sound would pierce the air: 
And all around would stop and stare. 
Filling our hearts with joy and care;

We'd run to the cabin, our feet light as air,

The siren still brings memories everlasting.

5 May 2013 Ahmedabad to Sarangpur On that bright sunny morning in Ahmedabad, Bapa, you took us all by surprise! There were no special or specific programmes planned for that day. Yes, it was Sunday, so Sunday sabha in the evening at Shahibaug Mandir. Yes…

The day you arrived in Sarangpur, a place which you considered your home.

That small village in India became the centre of our universe for those years.

The joy was palpable that day in the hearts of all, and you even greeted your beloved Mahant Swami on that day.

You were used to travelling from village to village.

In 1981, you visited over 450 villages.
In 1985, you visited over 344 places.
In 1990, you visited over 260 places.

From visiting multiple villages every single day, now, all of a sudden, you were in only one place.

But you were never disturbed. Only forever joyful.

You would personally meet hundreds of thousands. You were the ‘people’s guru’. Living your every second, of every day, amidst devotees.

And now you would spend most of your day in your room surrounded only by a handful of swamis.

But you were never lonely, never sorrowful. 

You always remained happy due to the bliss of God you forever experienced.

Never asking: ‘How are things running?’, ‘Is everything OK?, ‘Is the Akshardham we built in Delhi running okay?’, ‘Is the mandir we built in London still attracting visitors?’

No, not a single question. You trusted those you had guided, nurtured, and appointed.
You did everything, but never owned anything.
You built this entire global spiritual fellowship from the ground up, but were attached to only God. 

From inspecting plans and examining stones, you were now waving chhadis and throwing balls. But you were still joyful.

And yes, we will forever sing songs of your glory of those glorious days when you were an active and unstoppable force walking from house to house, and leading so many projects worldwide. 

But amazingly, we will also fondly remember these years when you were bound to a wheelchair.

Because you were our Bapa. Still the same smile, the same radiance, and the same inspiration.
Humility. As a teenager, Shastriji Maharaj had taught you to fold your hands, and in that same Sarangpur - 75 years later - until the very end, you kept your hands forever folded.

Those electric moments will stay with us forever. You brought an explosion of joy, energy, positivity, devotion, spirituality. Pure vibes.

You gave us darshan and bliss in so many ways. Obliging to every single request. Garlands, Hindolo, Rangotsav, Shakotsav, instruments - the list is endless. But you continued doing what you did your entire life - selflessly giving to others.

What was the secret of your bliss? 
When you were barely able to speak, and when you were frail, there was one thing which nobody could ever deny. 
Your everlasting devotion to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and your gurus. 

It was so deep, so entrenched into your very existence, it was who you were, at your very core. The conversations we see in the above videos reveal this so starkly.

And how can we ever forget your smile and laughter. It was divine. Infectious.

You were the Satpurush, Aksharbrahma, Bhagwan-na akhand dharak sant. A being of a completely different realm. 

But at the same time, you were an adorable human - so loveable, so delightful, so innocent, so perfect. 

The ultimate combination of divinity and humanity.
And in those years, there were so many divine moments where you also expressed your love for Pujya Mahant Swami...

Beauty. 
He was beautiful, but not like the way we talk of other humans in the world. 
He was beautiful for the way he thought. 
He was beautiful for the sparkle in his eyes when he talked about the Guru and God he loved. 
He was beautiful for his ability to make other people smile, even when he was frail and ill. 
No, he wasn't only beautiful for the radiance of his face. 
He was beautiful, for his every virtue, for every part of who he was.
And he was our guru. 
Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Bapa.

Age, circumstances, the scale of his achievements over all these decades, even the condition of his own body could massively change, but nothing could sway him from his ishta-bhakti. That remained unchanging, because that is who he was, at his core. The same ishta-bhakti he had throughout his life, was the same ishta-bhakti he had in the final year of his life, when his hands could barely move, but he'd still always reach out for his beloved Thakorji, because that devotion to God was never something he learnt or cultivated; it was who he was.

For many around the world, this ‘Akshardhamno kol’ is etched in our hearts as a permanent reminder of the everlasting peace that the Satpurush can grant. Despite the many challenges, hardships, and miseries life can bring, in such moments, the Satpurush can grant us with bliss. Such reassurances fill hearts with joy and security and make so many fearless in the face of death, disease, disappointment, and despair.

Years later, Shastriji Maharaj had selected this sacred location. After procuring the bungalow here, he consecrated a miraculous murti of Lalji Maharaj in 1949. 

Gradually, more land was acquired and plans for a shikharbaddha mandir were finalised. A beautiful mandir was constructed, and on 10 May 1962, Yogiji Maharaj performed the murti-pratishtha.

This mandir now serves as the international headquarters of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

16 May 1951 
Vaishakh sud 10

Gadhada Mandir Murti Pratishtha

In the town of Gadhpur sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan from 1805 to 1830, Shastriji Maharaj went to great efforts to fulfil Bhagwan Swaminarayan's sankalp of building a grand shikharbaddh mandir on the hillock on the banks of the River Ghela.

After 33 years of perseverance in trying to acquire the land, he eventually succeeded and performed the foundation stone-laying ceremony in 1949. He began the construction of a marble mandir and shortly before the scheduled pratishtha, he visited Gadhada despite being bedridden with illness in Sarangpur. 

On 12 April 1951, he bathed the murtis with water from the sacred River Ghela and performed the pratishtha rituals, before proclaiming: "My vidhi is now over. Jogi will come and perform the [final pratishtha] arti."

Six days following the passing of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj performed the pran-pratishtha ceremony of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta in the central shrine of the grand marble mandir on 16 May 1951.

18 May 2001
Vaishakh vad 10, VS 2057
Sankari, India

Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated and performed the murti-pratishtha at the new BAPS mandir in Sankari.

Sankari is a very small village with a population of no more than a hundred people and a single street of homes. 

The first shikharbaddh mandir consecrated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in this village in 1971. 

Over the decades, the efforts of Swamishri and sadhus saw Satsang flourish in the region of Sankari. They travelled to the tribal villages and inspired thousands to give up addictions and superstitions. The Sankari mandir soon burgeoned into a centre for spiritual and moral regeneration. 

In 1988, a portion of the mandir land was transformed for over six months into an ideal cattle camp for the drought-stricken cattle. 

Every Punam, 6,000 to 7,000 devotees would come for darshan.

With the growing magnitude of Satsang, the need for a larger mandir complex became necessary. To satisfy the increasing needs, Swamishri performed the ground-breaking ceremony for a new shikharbaddh mandir on 15 January 1996. Within 5 years, the intricately carved mandir made of pink sandstone was ready.

The inauguration ceremony of the newly built mandir was performed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj on 18 May 2001.

19 May 2016 was the final time he would come to give darshan from the glass cabin known as 'Pramukh Mandiram'.

Today, we remember his willpower, love, divinity, and radiance. 21 May 1950 
Jeth sud 4
Pramukh Varni Din

On this day in Ambli Vali Pol in Amdavad, Shastriji Maharaj made 28-year-old Shastri Narayanswarupdas the president (Pramukh) of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

And from that moment, the course of history shifted.
A moment not just historic for BAPS, but historic for humanity.
This was not merely the appointment of a spiritual head.
It was the beginning of a revolution in compassion, integrity, and faith.

Today was the day the name ‘Pramukh Swami’ was born – a name that would live in the hearts of millions.

He built more than 1,200 mandirs.
He ordained over 1,000 sadhus.
He established schools, hospitals, and so much more.
He transformed hearts and homes.

But more than what he built, it is how he built it.
With no pride. No ownership. Only devotion.

At the heart of it all was a pledge.
A vow he made to his guru Shastriji Maharaj on this day.
He never cared for his body, and served till his very last breath.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj redefined leadership, not as command but as care.

“In the joy of others lies our own.”
He lived it. He taught it. 
And everywhere he went, he left it behind as a gift to humanity.

Today, 76 years on, we bow our heads and lift our hearts in reverence
To a saint who never asked to lead.
But through love, changed our world.

Anand

It was during this time that Yogiji Maharaj stayed for six days in Anand and visited the home of Manilal Naranbhai Patel, whose young son came in touch with Yogiji Maharaj for the very first time.

It was a life-changing spiritual experience for the 17-year-old Vinubhai. Soon after this, he was so moved by the saintliness of Yogiji Maharaj, that he longed to spend every spare moment in his guru's company.

From 1951 to 1957, young Vinubhai often rushed to Yogiji Maharaj during his vacations. He was totally won over by Yogiji Maharaj’s selfless love, and he was determined to offer his all at the feet of Yogiji Maharaj.

This eventually culminated in Yogiji Maharaj ordaining Vinubhai as a parshad in February 1957.
